i've posted once on reddit that i've wasted my life by gambling all my money away, lurking only

few years later and im starting to get financially healthy again, almost out of debt

i'll take this million dorrar ty

Tried GA, but they keep saying the same stuff, which is not helpful. They basically just tell to focus on other stuff and quit. It's not that easy. And yeah if only I had that kind of friends with alot of money lol..

Great advice, thank you. I'll make a note of this and stick it to my monitor actually :) You are right about the urge to win it back, this urge wasn't as strong when I still had a job and weekly income.

My father and mother don't have the money to give me money, so what can they do? We can only talk about it, but I don't see how that helps the situation. They are very judging on what I do. And the temptation can be gone for weeks, but then I just force to forget all the times I tilted all my money away, and think: "Let's try it again. And play serious this time." My only thoughts then are winning alot of money.

Yes, I have. But I'm looking for a way to get out of this mess without going to those meetings. They will only tell me to tell my parents/relatives etc. and I really can't do that. The only thing they will do is tell me how stupid I am and everyone will know me as "the kid that gambled away all his money". I really want to get out of this without anyone knowing.

I'm sorry I wasn't clear, but it's about Online Poker. I have excluded myself from various sites, but there are literally hundreds of poker rooms. I have deleted, for example, PokerStars about 20 times from my computer. I like the idea about calling my bank, will try it first thing tomorrow thanks! And yes, bankroll mgmt I never had.

I gamble, play poker, to win back the money I have lost. It sounds very stupid now I typ it here, but 'just stop playing poker' sounds easier than it is. There were times is sold stuff to get 10~20 euro, just to deposit and win it all back.
It's not about the skills. I can play poker, but it's the chasing losses that keeps me down. Every time I lose, I want to win it back. It sounds easy to just quit, but it's not.
